nodes.name: Ces\`{a}ro operator $Cf$
nodes.statement: Given a locally integrable function $f:[0,\infty)\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$, {\it the Ces\`{a}ro operator Cf} is defined by $$(Cf)(x):=\frac{1}{x}\int_0^{x}f(t)dt, \qquad x\in(0,\infty).$$
nodes.statement_short: Ces\`{a}ro operator: the running average $\frac{1}{x}\int_0^x f$ of a locally integrable function on $(0,\infty)$.

nodes.name: fuzzy number; space $E^1$
nodes.statement: A \textit{fuzzy number} is a fuzzy set on the real axis, i.e. u is normal, fuzzy convex, upper semi-continuous and $\operatorname{supp}u =\overline{\{t\in\mathbb{R}:u(t)>0\}}$ is compact \cite{zadeh}. We denote the space of fuzzy numbers by $E^1$.
nodes.statement_short: A fuzzy number is a normal, fuzzy convex, upper semi-continuous fuzzy set on $\mathbb{R}$ with compact support; their space is $E^1$.
nodes.genus: a fuzzy set on the real axis

nodes.name: $\alpha$-level set $[u]_{\alpha}$
nodes.statement: \textit{$\alpha$-level set} $[u]_{\alpha}$ of $u\in E^1$ is defined by \begin{eqnarray*} [u]_{\alpha}:=\left\{\begin{array}{ccc} \{t\in\mathbb{R}:u(t)\geq\alpha\} & , & \qquad if \quad 0<\alpha\leq 1, \\[6 pt] \overline{\{t\in\mathbb{R}:u(t)>\alpha\}} & , & if \quad \alpha=0.\end{array} \right. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: The $\alpha$-level set of a fuzzy number is its $\alpha$-superlevel set for $\alpha\in(0,1]$, and the closure of the strict $0$-superlevel set for $\alpha=0$.

nodes.name: crisp fuzzy number $\overline{r}$
nodes.statement: Each $r\in\mathbb{R}$ can be regarded as a fuzzy number $\overline{r}$ defined by \begin{eqnarray*} \overline{r}(t):=\left\{\begin{array}{ccc} 1 & , & if \quad t=r, \\ 0 & , & if \quad t\neq r.\end{array} \right. \end{eqnarray*}

nodes.name: addition and scalar multiplication on $E^1$
nodes.statement: Let $u,v\in E^1$ and $k\in\mathbb{R}$. The addition and scalar multiplication are defined by \begin{eqnarray*} [u+v]_{\alpha}=[u]_{\alpha} +[v]_{\alpha}=[u^-_{\alpha}+v^-_{\alpha}, u^+_{\alpha}+v^+_{\alpha}], [k u]_{\alpha}=k[u]_{\alpha} \end{eqnarray*} where $[u]_{\alpha}=[u^-_{\alpha}, u^+_{\alpha}]$, for all $\alpha\in[0,1]$.
nodes.statement_short: Addition and scalar multiplication of fuzzy numbers are defined levelwise on the $\alpha$-level intervals.

nodes.name: metric $D$ on $E^1$
nodes.statement: The metric $D$ on $E^1$ is defined as \begin{eqnarray*} D(u,v):=\sup_{\alpha\in[0,1]}d([u]_{\alpha},[v]_{\alpha}):= \sup_{\alpha\in[0,1]}\max\{|u^-_{\alpha}-v^-_{\alpha}|,|u^+_{\alpha}- v^+_{\alpha}|\}. \end{eqnarray*} where $d$ is the Hausdorff metric.
nodes.statement_short: $D$ is the supremum over $\alpha\in[0,1]$ of the Hausdorff distance between the $\alpha$-level intervals.

nodes.name: partial ordering $\preceq$ on $E^1$
nodes.statement: Partial ordering relation on $E^1$ is defined as follows: \begin{eqnarray*} u\preceq v \Longleftrightarrow [u]_{\alpha}\preceq[v]_{\alpha}\Longleftrightarrow u^-_{\alpha}\leq v^-_{\alpha}~\text{ and }~u^+_{\alpha}\leq v^+_{\alpha}~\text{ for all }~\alpha\in[0,1]. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: $u\preceq v$ iff both endpoints of every $\alpha$-level interval of $u$ are $\leq$ those of $v$.

nodes.name: negative fuzzy number
nodes.statement: We say a fuzzy number $u$ is negative if and only if $u(t)=0$ for all $t\geq 0$ (see \cite{negative}).

nodes.name: continuity of a fuzzy-number-valued function
nodes.statement: A fuzzy-number-valued function $f:[a,b]\to E^1$ is said to be continuous at $x_0\in [a,b]$ if for each $\varepsilon>0$ there is a $\delta>0$ such that $D(f(x), f(x_0))<\varepsilon$ whenever $x\in [a,b]$ with $|x-x_0|<\delta$. If $f(x)$ is continuous at each $x\in [a,b]$, then we say $f(x)$ is continuous on $[a,b]$.
nodes.statement_short: Usual $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ continuity for fuzzy-number-valued functions, measured in the metric $D$.
differentia: for each $\varepsilon>0$ there is a $\delta>0$ such that $D(f(x), f(x_0))<\varepsilon$ whenever $x\in [a,b]$ with $|x-x_0|<\delta$

nodes.name: Riemann integrable fuzzy-valued function
nodes.statement: \cite{gv} A fuzzy-valued function $f:[a,b]\to E^1$ is called Riemann integrable on $[a,b]$, if there exists $I\in E^1$ with the property : $\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists\delta>0$ such that for any division of $[a,b]$ $d : a=x_0<x_1<\cdots<x_n=b$ of norm $v(d)<\delta$, and for any points $\xi_i\in[x_i,x_{i+1}]\ i=\overline{0,n-1}$, we have $$D\left(\sum\limits_{i=0}^{n-1}f(\xi_i)(x_{i+1}-x_i), I\right)<\varepsilon.$$ Then $I=\int\limits_a^bf(x)dx$.
nodes.statement_short: Riemann integrability of a fuzzy-valued function: Riemann sums converge in the metric $D$ to a fuzzy number $I=\int_a^b f$.
differentia: there exists $I\in E^1$ with the property : $\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists\delta>0$ such that for any division of $[a,b]$ $d : a=x_0<x_1<\cdots<x_n=b$ of norm $v(d)<\delta$, and for any points $\xi_i\in[x_i,x_{i+1}]\ i=\overline{0,n-1}$, we have $D\left(\sum\limits_{i=0}^{n-1}f(\xi_i)(x_{i+1}-x_i), I\right)<\varepsilon$

nodes.name: improper integral of a fuzzy-number-valued function on $[a,\infty)$
nodes.statement: Suppose $f(x)$ is a fuzzy-number-valued function defined on the unbounded interval $[a, \infty)$. Then we define \begin{eqnarray*} \int_a^{\infty}f(x)dx=\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_a^{t}f(x)dx \end{eqnarray*} provided the limit on the right-hand side exists in $E^1$, in which case we say the integral converges and is equal to the value of limit. Otherwise, we say the integral diverges.
nodes.statement_short: The improper fuzzy integral $\int_a^\infty f$ is the $E^1$-limit of $\int_a^t f$; it converges when that limit exists and diverges otherwise.
nodes.genus: limit of proper fuzzy Riemann integrals
differentia: provided the limit on the right-hand side exists in $E^1$

nodes.name: Ces\`{a}ro means $\sigma(t)$ of $s(t)$
nodes.statement: \begin{eqnarray} \sigma(t)=\frac{1}{t}\int_0^{t}s(u)du, \qquad t\in(0,\infty). \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Definition formula of the Ces\`{a}ro mean $\sigma(t)$ of the integral function $s$.

nodes.name: the improper integral $\int_0^{\infty}f(x)dx$ under study
nodes.statement: \begin{eqnarray} \int_0^{\infty}f(x)dx \end{eqnarray}

nodes.name: Ces\`{a}ro summability of integrals of fuzzy-number-valued functions
nodes.statement: Let $f:[0,\infty)\rightarrow E^1$ be a continuous fuzzy-number-valued function  and $s(t)=\int\limits_0^{t}f(x)dx$. The Ces\`{a}ro means of $s(t)$ are defined by \begin{eqnarray} \sigma(t)=\frac{1}{t}\int_0^{t}s(u)du, \qquad t\in(0,\infty). \end{eqnarray} The integral \begin{eqnarray} \int_0^{\infty}f(x)dx \end{eqnarray} is said to be Ces\`{a}ro summable to a fuzzy number L if $\lim_{t\to \infty}\sigma(t)=L$. The value of this limit is said to be the Ces\`{a}ro sum of the integral.
nodes.statement_short: $\int_0^\infty f$ is Ces\`{a}ro summable to $L$ when the means $\sigma(t)=\frac{1}{t}\int_0^t s(u)du$ of $s(t)=\int_0^t f$ tend to $L$.
nodes.definiendum: Ces\`{a}ro summable to a fuzzy number L
nodes.genus: improper integral $\int_0^{\infty}f(x)dx$ of a continuous fuzzy-number-valued function

nodes.name: slowly decreasing fuzzy-number-valued function
nodes.statement: A fuzzy-number-valued function $s(x)$ is said to be slowly decreasing if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $t_0\geq 0$ and $\lambda >1$ such that \begin{eqnarray*} s(x)\succeq s(t)- \overline{\varepsilon} \end{eqnarray*} whenever $t_0<t<x\leq \lambda t.$
nodes.statement_short: Fuzzy analogue of Schmidt-type slow decrease: $s(x)$ cannot drop below $s(t)-\overline{\varepsilon}$ on multiplicative windows $t<x\leq\lambda t$.
differentia: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $t_0\geq 0$ and $\lambda >1$ such that $s(x)\succeq s(t)- \overline{\varepsilon}$ whenever $t_0<t<x\leq \lambda t$

nodes.name: Ces\`{a}ro summability of a fuzzy-number-valued function
nodes.statement: A continuous fuzzy-number-valued function $f:[0,\infty)\rightarrow E^1$ is said to be Ces\`{a}ro summable to a fuzzy number $L$ if \begin{eqnarray*} \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{1}{t}\int_0^{t}f(x)dx=L. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: A continuous fuzzy-number-valued function is Ces\`{a}ro summable to $L$ if its running averages $\frac{1}{t}\int_0^t f$ converge to $L$.
nodes.definiendum: Ces\`{a}ro summable to a fuzzy number $L$

nodes.name: Landau type one-sided condition $xf(x)\succeq u$
nodes.statement: \begin{eqnarray} xf(x)\succeq u \quad \textrm{for}\quad x>x_0, \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: One-sided Landau condition: $xf(x)$ stays above a fixed negative fuzzy number $u$ for large $x$.

nodes.name: M\'{o}ricz reformulated slow decrease condition
nodes.statement: At this point we recall the reformulated condition of M$\acute{o}$ricz \cite{moric1} for a slowly decreasing real valued function $f$ such that \begin{eqnarray} \lim_{\lambda\rightarrow 1^{-}}\liminf_{t\rightarrow\infty}\min_{\lambda t\leq x\leq t}[f(t)-f(x)]\geq0. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Real-valued slow decrease restated as $\lim_{\lambda\to1^-}\liminf_{t\to\infty}\min_{\lambda t\leq x\leq t}[f(t)-f(x)]\geq 0$.

nodes.name: Algebraic properties of $(E^1,+,\cdot)$ (Bede--Gal)
nodes.statement: \cite{bede} The following statements hold: \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] $\overline{0} \in E^{1}$ is neutral element with respect to $+$, i.e., $u+\overline{0}=\overline{0}+u=u$ for all $u \in E^{1}$. \item [(ii)] With respect to $\overline{0}$, none of $u \neq \overline{r}$, $r\in \mathbb{R}$ has opposite in $E^{1}.$ \item[(iii)] For any $a,b \in\mathbb{R}$ with $a, b \geq 0$ or $a,b \leq 0$ and any $u\in E^{1}$, we have $(a + b) u = au + bu$. For general $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, the above property does not hold. \item[(iv)] For any $a \in \mathbb{R}$ and any $u, v \in E^{1}$, we have $a (u+ v) = au + av.$ \item[(v)] For any $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ and any $u \in E^{1}$, we have $a (b u) = (a b) u.$ \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: $E^1$ has neutral element $\overline{0}$, no additive inverses for non-crisp $u$, same-sign distributivity, distributivity over $+$, and associativity of scalar products.
conclusions: With respect to $\overline{0}$, none of $u \neq \overline{r}$, $r\in \mathbb{R}$ has opposite in $E^{1}.$

nodes.name: Metric properties of $(E^1,D)$ (Bede--Gal)
nodes.statement: \cite{bede} Let $u,v,w,z\in E^1$ and $k\in\mathbb{R}$. Then, \begin{itemize} \item [(i)] $(E^1,D)$ is a complete metric space. \item [(ii)] $D(ku,kv)=|k|D(u,v)$. \item [(iii)] $D(u+v,w+v)=D(u,w)$. \item [(iv)] $D(u+v,w+z)\leq D(u,w)+D(v,z)$. \item [(v)] $|D(u,\overline{0})-D(v,\overline{0})|\leq D(u,v)\leq D(u,\overline{0})+D(v,\overline{0})$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: $(E^1,D)$ is complete, $D$ is absolutely homogeneous, translation invariant, subadditive, and satisfies a two-sided triangle bound against $\overline{0}$.

nodes.name: $\varepsilon$-comparison lemma for fuzzy numbers
nodes.statement: Let $u,v,w,e\in E^1$ and $\varepsilon>0$. The following statements hold: \begin{itemize} \item [(i)] $D(u,v)\leq\varepsilon$ if and only if $u-\overline{\varepsilon}\preceq v \preceq u+\overline{\varepsilon}$ \item [(ii)] If $u\preceq v +\overline{\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$,  then $u\preceq v$. \item [(iii)] If $u\preceq v$ and $v\preceq w$, then $u\preceq w$. \item [(iv)] If  $u\preceq w$ and $v\preceq e$, then $u+v\preceq w+e$. \item [(v)] If  $u+w\preceq v+ w$ then $u\preceq v$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Dictionary between the metric $D$ and the order $\preceq$: $\varepsilon$-closeness equals two-sided $\overline{\varepsilon}$-sandwiching, plus transitivity, additivity and cancellation of $\preceq$.
nodes.origin_citation: Aytar, Mammadov & Pehlivan 2006; Aytar & Pehlivan 2007; Li & Wu 2007; Talo & Ba\c{s}ar 2013
conclusions: $D(u,v)\leq\varepsilon$ if and only if $u-\overline{\varepsilon}\preceq v \preceq u+\overline{\varepsilon}$
If $u\preceq v +\overline{\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$,  then $u\preceq v$.
If $u\preceq v$ and $v\preceq w$, then $u\preceq w$.
If  $u\preceq w$ and $v\preceq e$, then $u+v\preceq w+e$.

nodes.name: Existence and levelwise parametrization of the fuzzy Riemann integral (Goetschel--Voxman)
nodes.statement: \cite{gv} If the fuzzy-number-valued function $f:[a,b]\to E^1$ is continuous (with respect to the metric D) and for each $x\in[a,b]$, $f(x)$ has the parametric representation $$[f(x)]_{\alpha}=[f_{\alpha}^-(x), f_{\alpha}^+(x)],$$ then $\int\limits_a^bf(x)dx$ exists, belongs to $E^1$ and is parametrized by $$\left[\int\limits_a^bf(x)dx\right]_{\alpha}=\left[\int\limits_a^bf_{\alpha}^-(x)dx, \int\limits_a^bf_{\alpha}^+(x)dx\right].$$
nodes.statement_short: For continuous $f$, the fuzzy integral exists in $E^1$ and its $\alpha$-levels are the ordinary integrals of the level endpoint functions.
assumptions: the fuzzy-number-valued function $f:[a,b]\to E^1$ is continuous (with respect to the metric D)
for each $x\in[a,b]$, $f(x)$ has the parametric representation $$[f(x)]_{\alpha}=[f_{\alpha}^-(x), f_{\alpha}^+(x)],$$
conclusions: $\int\limits_a^bf(x)dx$ exists, belongs to $E^1$ and is parametrized by $$\left[\int\limits_a^bf(x)dx\right]_{\alpha}=\left[\int\limits_a^bf_{\alpha}^-(x)dx, \int\limits_a^bf_{\alpha}^+(x)dx\right].$$

nodes.name: Basic properties of the fuzzy Riemann integral (after Anastassiou)
nodes.statement: If $f:[a,b]\to E^1$ and $g:[a,b]\to E^1$ are continuous then \item [(i)] $\int\limits_a^b(\alpha f(x)+\beta g(x))dx=\alpha \int\limits_a^bf(x)dx+\beta\int\limits_a^bg(x)dx$ where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are real numbers. \item [(ii)] $\int\limits_a^bf(x)dx=\int\limits_a^cf(x)dx+\int\limits_c^bf(x)dx$ where $a<c<b$. \item [(iii)]The function $F :[a,b]\to \mathbb{R_+}$ defined by $F(x)=D(f(x),g(x))$ is continuous on $[a, b]$ and\\ $$D\left(\int\limits_a^bf(x)dx,\int\limits_a^bg(x)dx \right)\leq \int\limits_a^bF(x)dx.$$ \item [(iv)] $\int\limits_a^xf(t)dt$ is a continuous function in $x\in[a,b]$. \item [(v)] $\int\limits_a^b f(x)dx \preceq \int\limits_a^b g(x)dx $  whenever   $f(x)\preceq g(x)$ for all $x\in[a,b]$.
nodes.statement_short: Linearity, additivity over subintervals, a $D$-integral triangle inequality, continuity of the primitive, and monotonicity of the fuzzy integral.
conclusions: The function $F :[a,b]\to \mathbb{R_+}$ defined by $F(x)=D(f(x),g(x))$ is continuous on $[a, b]$ and $D\left(\int\limits_a^bf(x)dx,\int\limits_a^bg(x)dx \right)\leq \int\limits_a^bF(x)dx.$

nodes.name: Regularity of Ces\`{a}ro summability of integrals
nodes.statement: If the integral (\ref{integral}) converges to a fuzzy number L, then (\ref{ortalama}) also converges to L.
nodes.statement_short: Ces\`{a}ro summability of integrals is regular: convergence of $\int_0^\infty f$ to $L$ forces $\sigma(t)\to L$.
assumptions: the integral (\ref{integral}) converges to a fuzzy number L

nodes.name: Proof of the regularity theorem
nodes.statement: Let $$\lim\limits_{t\to \infty}s(t)=\int_0^{\infty}f(x)dx=L$$ for  some $L\in E^1$. Then given any $\varepsilon>0 $ there exists $t_0>0$ such that $D(s(t), L)<\frac{\varepsilon}{2}$ whenever $t\geq t_0$ and there exists $M>0$ such that $D(s(t), L)<M$ whenever $t< t_0$. So we have \begin{eqnarray*} D(\sigma(t),L)&=&D\left(\frac{1}{t}\int_0^ts(u)du, L\right) \\&=& D\left(\frac{1}{t}\int_0^ts(u)du,\frac{1}{t}\int_0^tLdu\right) \\&=& \frac{1}{t}D\left(\int_0^ts(u)du, \int_0^tLdu\right) \\&\leq & \frac{1}{t}\int_0^tD(s(u),L)du \\&=& \frac{1}{t}\int_0^{t_0}D(s(u),L)du+ \frac{1}{t}\int_{t_0}^tD(s(u),L)du \\&\leq & \frac{t_0M}{t}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\frac{(t-t_0)}{t}< \frac{t_0M}{t}+ \frac{\varepsilon}{2} \end{eqnarray*} Since $\lim\limits_{t\to\infty}\frac{t_0M}{t}=0$, there exists $t_1>0$ such that $\left|\frac{t_0M}{t}\right|<\frac{\varepsilon}{2}$ whenever $t\geq t_1$. So there exists $t_2=\max\{t_0,t_1\}$ such that $$D(\sigma(t),L)<\varepsilon$$ whenever $t\geq t_2$. This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Direct $\varepsilon/2$ splitting of $\frac{1}{t}\int_0^t D(s(u),L)du$ at $t_0$, bounding the initial piece by $t_0M/t\to0$.

nodes.name: Fix $L$ and choose $t_0$, $M$
nodes.statement: Let $$\lim\limits_{t\to \infty}s(t)=\int_0^{\infty}f(x)dx=L$$ for  some $L\in E^1$. Then given any $\varepsilon>0 $ there exists $t_0>0$ such that $D(s(t), L)<\frac{\varepsilon}{2}$ whenever $t\geq t_0$ and there exists $M>0$ such that $D(s(t), L)<M$ whenever $t< t_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Set up: use convergence of $s$ to get an $\varepsilon/2$ tail bound past $t_0$ and a crude bound $M$ before $t_0$.

nodes.name: Estimate $D(\sigma(t),L)$
nodes.statement: So we have \begin{eqnarray*} D(\sigma(t),L)&=&D\left(\frac{1}{t}\int_0^ts(u)du, L\right) \\&=& D\left(\frac{1}{t}\int_0^ts(u)du,\frac{1}{t}\int_0^tLdu\right) \\&=& \frac{1}{t}D\left(\int_0^ts(u)du, \int_0^tLdu\right) \\&\leq & \frac{1}{t}\int_0^tD(s(u),L)du \\&=& \frac{1}{t}\int_0^{t_0}D(s(u),L)du+ \frac{1}{t}\int_{t_0}^tD(s(u),L)du \\&\leq & \frac{t_0M}{t}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\frac{(t-t_0)}{t}< \frac{t_0M}{t}+ \frac{\varepsilon}{2} \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Push $D$ inside the integral, split at $t_0$, and bound the two pieces by $t_0M/t$ and $\varepsilon/2$.

nodes.name: Absorb $t_0M/t$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Since $\lim\limits_{t\to\infty}\frac{t_0M}{t}=0$, there exists $t_1>0$ such that $\left|\frac{t_0M}{t}\right|<\frac{\varepsilon}{2}$ whenever $t\geq t_1$. So there exists $t_2=\max\{t_0,t_1\}$ such that $$D(\sigma(t),L)<\varepsilon$$ whenever $t\geq t_2$. This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude $D(\sigma(t),L)<\varepsilon$ for $t\geq t_2=\max\{t_0,t_1\}$.

nodes.name: Converse of the regularity theorem fails
nodes.statement: By the following example it can be easily seen that the converse statement of Theorem \ref{regular} is not true in general.

nodes.name: Divergent but Ces\`{a}ro summable fuzzy integral
nodes.statement: Take the fuzzy-number-valued function  $f: [0,\infty) \to E^1$  such that {\small\begin{eqnarray*} (f(x))(t)= \begin{cases} (t-\cos x).(x+1)^2, & \quad \textrm{if} \quad  \cos x\leq t\leq \cos x+\frac{1}{(1+x)^2}, \\ 2-(t-\cos x).(x+1)^2, &  \quad \textrm{if} \quad \cos x+\frac{1}{(1+x)^2}\leq t\leq \cos x+\frac{2}{(1+x)^2}, \\ 0, & \qquad  \quad \textrm{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{eqnarray*}} Then $f$ is continuous and {\small\begin{eqnarray*} f^-_{\alpha}(x)=\cos x+\frac{\alpha}{(x+1)^2}\qquad\qquad &,&\qquad\qquad f^+_{\alpha}(x)=\cos x+\frac{2-\alpha}{(x+1)^2}\\ \int_{0}^{t}f_{\alpha}^-(x)dx=sint+\alpha\left(1-\frac{1}{t+1}\right)\quad &,& \quad \int_{0}^{t}f_{\alpha}^+(x)dx=sint+(2-\alpha)\left(1-\frac{1}{t+1}\right) \end{eqnarray*}} Obviously $\int\limits_{0}^{\infty}f(x)dx$ is divergent. To calculate Ces\`{a}ro mean, considering (\ref{ortalama}) we have {\small\begin{eqnarray*} \sigma_{\alpha}^-(t)&=&\frac{1}{t}\int_0^{t}s_{\alpha}^-(u)du=\frac{1}{t}\int_0^{t}\left(\int_0^{u}f_{\alpha}^-(x)dx\right)du=-\frac{\cos t}{t}+\frac{1}{t}+\alpha\left(1-\frac{\ln (t+1)}{t}\right)\\ \sigma_{\alpha}^+(t)&=&\frac{1}{t}\int_0^{t}s_{\alpha}^+(u)du=\frac{1}{t}\int_0^{t}\left(\int_0^{u}f_{\alpha}^+(x)dx\right)du=-\frac{\cos t}{t}+\frac{1}{t}+(2-\alpha)\left(1-\frac{\ln (t+1)}{t}\right). \end{eqnarray*}} So we get \begin{eqnarray*} \begin{rcases} \lim_{t\to \infty}\sigma_{\alpha}^-(t)=\alpha \\ \lim_{t\to \infty}\sigma_{\alpha}^+(t)=2-\alpha\end{rcases} \qquad [u]_{\alpha}=[\alpha, 2-\alpha] \qquad and \qquad \lim_{t\to \infty}D(\sigma(t),u)=0. \end{eqnarray*} Then $\int\limits_{0}^{\infty}f(x)dx$ is Ces\`{a}ro summable to fuzzy number $u$ such that \begin{eqnarray*} u(t)= \begin{cases} \ \ t &\quad \textrm{if} \quad  0\leq t\leq 1, \\ 2-t &  \quad \textrm{if} \quad 1\leq t\leq 2, \\ \ \ 0 & \quad \quad  \ \  \textrm{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: A triangular fuzzy function built on $\cos x$ whose improper integral diverges yet is Ces\`{a}ro summable to the triangular fuzzy number on $[0,2]$.

nodes.name: Two-window decomposition identities for Ces\`{a}ro means
nodes.statement: If $s$ be a continuous fuzzy-number-valued function then for every $\lambda>1$ \begin{eqnarray} \frac{1}{\lambda t-t}\int_t^{\lambda t}s(x)dx + \frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(t)=\sigma(\lambda t)+\frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(\lambda t) \end{eqnarray} and for every $0<\ell<1$ \begin{eqnarray} \frac{1}{t-\ell t}\int_{\ell t}^{ t}s(x)dx + \frac{\ell}{1-\ell}\sigma(\ell t)=\sigma( t)+\frac{\ell}{1-\ell}\sigma(t). \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Kronecker-type identities expressing the window average of $s$ over $[t,\lambda t]$ (resp. $[\ell t,t]$) via Ces\`{a}ro means at $t$ and $\lambda t$ (resp. $\ell t$ and $t$).

nodes.name: Proof of the two-window decomposition identities
nodes.statement: Let $s$ be a continuous fuzzy-number-valued function. Then for every $\lambda>1$ we have \begin{eqnarray*} \sigma(\lambda t)+\frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(\lambda t)&=&\frac{\lambda}{\lambda-1}\sigma(\lambda t) \\&=& \frac{\lambda}{\lambda-1}\frac{1}{\lambda t}\int_0^{\lambda t}s(x)dx \\&=& \frac{1}{(\lambda-1)t}\left\{\int_0^{t}s(x)dx+\int_t^{\lambda t}s(x)dx\right\} \\&=& \frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(t)+ \frac{1}{t(\lambda -1)}\int_t^{\lambda t}s(x)dx \end{eqnarray*} by Lemma \ref{added} and Theorem \ref{bessart}. On the other hand for every $0<\ell<1$, using Lemma \ref{added} and Theorem \ref{bessart} again,  we get \begin{eqnarray*} \sigma( t)+\frac{\ell}{1-\ell}\sigma(t)&=&\frac{1}{1-\ell}\sigma( t) \\&=& \frac{1}{1-\ell}\frac{1}{t}\int_0^{ t}s(x)dx \\&=& \frac{1}{1-\ell}\frac{1}{t}\left\{\int_0^{\ell t}s(x)dx+\int_{\ell t}^{t}s(x)dx\right\} \\&=& \frac{\ell}{1-\ell}\frac{1}{\ell t}\int_0^{\ell t}s(x)dx+ \frac{1}{t(1-\ell)}\int_{\ell t}^{t}s(x)dx \\&=& \frac{\ell}{1-\ell}\sigma(\ell t)+ \frac{1}{t-\ell t}\int_{\ell t}^{ t}s(x)dx. \end{eqnarray*} So equalities (\ref{es1}) and (\ref{es2}) are satisfied.
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation: split $\int_0^{\lambda t}$ (resp. $\int_0^{t}$) at the inner endpoint using additivity of the fuzzy integral and same-sign distributivity in $E^1$.

nodes.name: Case $\lambda>1$: split $\int_0^{\lambda t}$ at $t$
nodes.statement: Let $s$ be a continuous fuzzy-number-valued function. Then for every $\lambda>1$ we have \begin{eqnarray*} \sigma(\lambda t)+\frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(\lambda t)&=&\frac{\lambda}{\lambda-1}\sigma(\lambda t) \\&=& \frac{\lambda}{\lambda-1}\frac{1}{\lambda t}\int_0^{\lambda t}s(x)dx \\&=& \frac{1}{(\lambda-1)t}\left\{\int_0^{t}s(x)dx+\int_t^{\lambda t}s(x)dx\right\} \\&=& \frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(t)+ \frac{1}{t(\lambda -1)}\int_t^{\lambda t}s(x)dx \end{eqnarray*} by Lemma \ref{added} and Theorem \ref{bessart}.
nodes.statement_short: Derive the $\lambda>1$ identity by additivity of the integral over $[0,t]\cup[t,\lambda t]$.

nodes.name: Case $0<\ell<1$: split $\int_0^{t}$ at $\ell t$
nodes.statement: On the other hand for every $0<\ell<1$, using Lemma \ref{added} and Theorem \ref{bessart} again,  we get \begin{eqnarray*} \sigma( t)+\frac{\ell}{1-\ell}\sigma(t)&=&\frac{1}{1-\ell}\sigma( t) \\&=& \frac{1}{1-\ell}\frac{1}{t}\int_0^{ t}s(x)dx \\&=& \frac{1}{1-\ell}\frac{1}{t}\left\{\int_0^{\ell t}s(x)dx+\int_{\ell t}^{t}s(x)dx\right\} \\&=& \frac{\ell}{1-\ell}\frac{1}{\ell t}\int_0^{\ell t}s(x)dx+ \frac{1}{t(1-\ell)}\int_{\ell t}^{t}s(x)dx \\&=& \frac{\ell}{1-\ell}\sigma(\ell t)+ \frac{1}{t-\ell t}\int_{\ell t}^{ t}s(x)dx. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Symmetric derivation of the $0<\ell<1$ identity by splitting at $\ell t$.

nodes.name: Conclude both identities
nodes.statement: So equalities (\ref{es1}) and (\ref{es2}) are satisfied.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude that both claimed equalities hold.

nodes.name: Window averages of $s$ converge to the Ces\`{a}ro sum
nodes.statement: If integral (\ref{integral}) is Ces\`{a}ro summable to a fuzzy number $L$, then for every $\lambda>1$ \begin{eqnarray} \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{1}{\lambda t-t}\int_t^{\lambda t}s(x)dx=L \end{eqnarray} and for every $0<\ell<1$ \begin{eqnarray} \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{1}{t-\ell t}\int_{\ell t}^{ t}s(x)dx =L. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: If $\int_0^\infty f$ is Ces\`{a}ro summable to $L$, the averages of $s$ over $[t,\lambda t]$ and $[\ell t,t]$ both tend to $L$.
assumptions: integral (\ref{integral}) is Ces\`{a}ro summable to a fuzzy number $L$

nodes.name: Necessary and sufficient Tauberian condition for Ces\`{a}ro summable fuzzy integrals
nodes.statement: Let fuzzy-number-valued function $f:[0,\infty)\rightarrow E^1$ be continuous. If integral (\ref{integral}) is Ces\`{a}ro summable to a fuzzy number L, then it converges to L if and only if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $t_0\geq 0$ and $\lambda>1$ such that for $t> t_0$ \begin{eqnarray} \frac{1}{\lambda t-t}\int_t^{\lambda t}s(x)dx \succeq s(t)-\overline{\varepsilon} \end{eqnarray} and another $0<\ell<1$ such that \begin{eqnarray} \frac{1}{t-\ell t}\int_{\ell t}^{ t}s(x)dx \preceq s(t)+\overline{\varepsilon}. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: A Ces\`{a}ro summable fuzzy integral converges to $L$ exactly when two one-sided window-average conditions on $s$ hold for large $t$.
assumptions: Let fuzzy-number-valued function $f:[0,\infty)\rightarrow E^1$ be continuous.
integral (\ref{integral}) is Ces\`{a}ro summable to a fuzzy number L
conclusions: it converges to L if and only if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $t_0\geq 0$ and $\lambda>1$ such that for $t> t_0$ $\frac{1}{\lambda t-t}\int_t^{\lambda t}s(x)dx \succeq s(t)-\overline{\varepsilon}$ and another $0<\ell<1$ such that $\frac{1}{t-\ell t}\int_{\ell t}^{ t}s(x)dx \preceq s(t)+\overline{\varepsilon}.$

nodes.name: Proof of the necessary and sufficient Tauberian condition
nodes.statement: {\it    Necessity}. Let the integral (\ref{integral}) converge to $L$. Using inequality \begin{eqnarray*} D\left(\frac{1}{\lambda t-t}\int_t^{\lambda t}s(x)dx, s(t)\right)\leq D\left(\frac{1}{\lambda t-t}\int_t^{\lambda t}s(x)dx, L\right)+D(L,s(t)), \end{eqnarray*} if we consider the equality (\ref{L1}) in Lemma \ref{lemma} then for $\lambda>1$ we obtain \begin{eqnarray*} \lim_{t\to \infty}D\left(\frac{1}{\lambda t-t}\int_t^{\lambda t}s(x)dx, s(t)\right)=0. \end{eqnarray*} For $0<\ell<1$, validity of (\ref{**}) can also be obtained analogously by using the equality (\ref{L2}) of Lemma \ref{lemma}. {\it    Sufficiency}. Assume that integral (\ref{integral}) is Ces\`{a}ro summable to $L$ and (\ref{*}), (\ref{**}) are satisfied. By (\ref{*}), there exist $t_1\geq 0$ and $\lambda>1$ such that for $t>t_1$ \begin{eqnarray*} \frac{1}{\lambda t-t}\int_t^{\lambda t}s(x)dx \succeq s(t)-\frac{\overline{\varepsilon}}{3}\ \cdot \end{eqnarray*} Besides since \begin{eqnarray*} \lim\limits_{t\to \infty}D\left(\frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(t), \frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(\lambda t)\right)=0, \end{eqnarray*} there exists $t_2\geq 0$ such that for $t>t_2$ \begin{eqnarray*} D\left(\frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(t), \frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(\lambda t)\right)\leq\frac{\varepsilon}{3}\cdot \end{eqnarray*} So by $(i)$ of Lemma \ref{epsilon} we get that \begin{eqnarray*} \frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(t)- \frac{\overline{\varepsilon}}{3}\preceq \frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(\lambda t)\preceq \frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(t)+ \frac{\overline{\varepsilon}}{3}. \end{eqnarray*} Also, since $\lim\limits_{t\to \infty}\sigma(\lambda t)=L$, there exists $t_3\geq 0$ such that  $D(\sigma(\lambda t), L)\leq\frac{\varepsilon}{3}$ for $t> t_3$, meaning \begin{eqnarray*} L- \frac{\overline{\varepsilon}}{3}\preceq \sigma(\lambda t)\preceq L + \frac{\overline{\varepsilon}}{3}\cdot \end{eqnarray*} Then considering the equality (\ref{es1}) , there exists $t_4=\max\{t_1, t_2, t_3\}$ such that for $t> t_4$ \begin{eqnarray*} s(t)-\frac{\overline{\varepsilon}}{3}+\frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(t)\preceq L + \frac{\overline{\varepsilon}}{3}+\frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(t)+ \frac{\overline{\varepsilon}}{3}\cdot \end{eqnarray*} So by $(v)$ of Lemma \ref{epsilon}, for $t> t_4$ we have \begin{eqnarray} s(t)\preceq L + \overline{\varepsilon} . \end{eqnarray} On the other hand, if we consider the condition (\ref{**}),  equality (\ref{es2}), Lemma \ref{epsilon} and proceed in a similar way as that above, we get that there exists a $t_4^*\geq 0$ such that for $t> t_4^*$ \begin{eqnarray} s(t)\succeq L - \overline{\varepsilon}. \end{eqnarray} Then combining inequalities (\ref{epsilon1}) and (\ref{epsilon2}), we obtain \begin{eqnarray*} L - \overline{\varepsilon}\preceq s(t)\preceq L + \overline{\varepsilon} \end{eqnarray*} whenever $t>\max\{t_4,t_4^*\}$ and this completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Necessity from Lemma window limits plus the triangle inequality; sufficiency by an $\varepsilon/3$ argument that feeds the decomposition identity into the order-cancellation lemma to sandwich $s(t)$ around $L$.

nodes.name: Necessity
nodes.statement: {\it    Necessity}. Let the integral (\ref{integral}) converge to $L$. Using inequality \begin{eqnarray*} D\left(\frac{1}{\lambda t-t}\int_t^{\lambda t}s(x)dx, s(t)\right)\leq D\left(\frac{1}{\lambda t-t}\int_t^{\lambda t}s(x)dx, L\right)+D(L,s(t)), \end{eqnarray*} if we consider the equality (\ref{L1}) in Lemma \ref{lemma} then for $\lambda>1$ we obtain \begin{eqnarray*} \lim_{t\to \infty}D\left(\frac{1}{\lambda t-t}\int_t^{\lambda t}s(x)dx, s(t)\right)=0. \end{eqnarray*} For $0<\ell<1$, validity of (\ref{**}) can also be obtained analogously by using the equality (\ref{L2}) of Lemma \ref{lemma}.
nodes.statement_short: Necessity: triangle inequality plus the window-average limits give $D(\text{window average}, s(t))\to 0$, hence both conditions.

nodes.name: Sufficiency setup: invoke condition (*) with $\varepsilon/3$
nodes.statement: {\it    Sufficiency}. Assume that integral (\ref{integral}) is Ces\`{a}ro summable to $L$ and (\ref{*}), (\ref{**}) are satisfied. By (\ref{*}), there exist $t_1\geq 0$ and $\lambda>1$ such that for $t>t_1$ \begin{eqnarray*} \frac{1}{\lambda t-t}\int_t^{\lambda t}s(x)dx \succeq s(t)-\frac{\overline{\varepsilon}}{3}\ \cdot \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Set up sufficiency: apply the first Tauberian condition with $\varepsilon/3$.

nodes.name: Sandwich $\frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(\lambda t)$ via Lemma (i)
nodes.statement: Besides since \begin{eqnarray*} \lim\limits_{t\to \infty}D\left(\frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(t), \frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(\lambda t)\right)=0, \end{eqnarray*} there exists $t_2\geq 0$ such that for $t>t_2$ \begin{eqnarray*} D\left(\frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(t), \frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(\lambda t)\right)\leq\frac{\varepsilon}{3}\cdot \end{eqnarray*} So by $(i)$ of Lemma \ref{epsilon} we get that \begin{eqnarray*} \frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(t)- \frac{\overline{\varepsilon}}{3}\preceq \frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(\lambda t)\preceq \frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(t)+ \frac{\overline{\varepsilon}}{3}. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Convert $\varepsilon/3$ metric closeness of the scaled means into an order sandwich using part (i) of the comparison lemma.

nodes.name: Sandwich $\sigma(\lambda t)$ around $L$
nodes.statement: Also, since $\lim\limits_{t\to \infty}\sigma(\lambda t)=L$, there exists $t_3\geq 0$ such that  $D(\sigma(\lambda t), L)\leq\frac{\varepsilon}{3}$ for $t> t_3$, meaning \begin{eqnarray*} L- \frac{\overline{\varepsilon}}{3}\preceq \sigma(\lambda t)\preceq L + \frac{\overline{\varepsilon}}{3}\cdot \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Use Ces\`{a}ro summability to sandwich $\sigma(\lambda t)$ within $\overline{\varepsilon}/3$ of $L$.

nodes.name: Combine with identity (es1) and cancel to get $s(t)\preceq L+\overline{\varepsilon}$
nodes.statement: Then considering the equality (\ref{es1}) , there exists $t_4=\max\{t_1, t_2, t_3\}$ such that for $t> t_4$ \begin{eqnarray*} s(t)-\frac{\overline{\varepsilon}}{3}+\frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(t)\preceq L + \frac{\overline{\varepsilon}}{3}+\frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(t)+ \frac{\overline{\varepsilon}}{3}\cdot \end{eqnarray*} So by $(v)$ of Lemma \ref{epsilon}, for $t> t_4$ we have \begin{eqnarray} s(t)\preceq L + \overline{\varepsilon} . \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Insert the $\lambda>1$ decomposition identity and cancel the common $\frac{1}{\lambda-1}\sigma(t)$ term to obtain the upper bound.

nodes.name: Symmetric argument gives $s(t)\succeq L-\overline{\varepsilon}$
nodes.statement: On the other hand, if we consider the condition (\ref{**}),  equality (\ref{es2}), Lemma \ref{epsilon} and proceed in a similar way as that above, we get that there exists a $t_4^*\geq 0$ such that for $t> t_4^*$ \begin{eqnarray} s(t)\succeq L - \overline{\varepsilon}. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the argument with the second condition and identity (es2) for the lower bound.

nodes.name: Combine the two bounds
nodes.statement: Then combining inequalities (\ref{epsilon1}) and (\ref{epsilon2}), we obtain \begin{eqnarray*} L - \overline{\varepsilon}\preceq s(t)\preceq L + \overline{\varepsilon} \end{eqnarray*} whenever $t>\max\{t_4,t_4^*\}$ and this completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude the two-sided sandwich $L-\overline{\varepsilon}\preceq s(t)\preceq L+\overline{\varepsilon}$, i.e. $s(t)\to L$.

nodes.name: Slow decrease equals equi-slow decrease of the level functions
nodes.statement: Fuzzy-number-valued function $s(x)$ is slowly decreasing if and only if the family of real valued functions $\{s^-_{\alpha}(x)\mid \alpha\in[0,1]\}$ and $\{s^+_{\alpha}(x)\mid \alpha\in[0,1]\}$ are equi-slowly decreasing i.e.  $\forall\varepsilon>0$ there exist $t_0\geq 0$ and $\lambda>1$ such that for all $\alpha\in[0,1]$ $$s_{\alpha}^-(x)-s_{\alpha}^-(t)\geq -\varepsilon \quad \textrm{and}\quad s_{\alpha}^+(x)-s_{\alpha}^+(t)\geq -\varepsilon \qquad \textrm{whenever} \quad t_0< t<x\leq \lambda t.$$
nodes.statement_short: Fuzzy slow decrease is equivalent to uniform ($\alpha$-independent) slow decrease of both families of level endpoint functions.

nodes.name: Left-window form of fuzzy slow decrease
nodes.statement: If the fuzzy-number-valued  function $s(x)$ is slowly decreasing, then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $t_0\geq0$ and  $0<\lambda<1$ such that for every $t>t_0$ \begin{eqnarray} s(t)\succeq s(x)-\overline{\varepsilon} \qquad \textrm{whenever}\qquad  \lambda t< x\leq t. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Slow decrease also yields the left-window inequality $s(t)\succeq s(x)-\overline{\varepsilon}$ for $\lambda t<x\leq t$ with $0<\lambda<1$.
assumptions: the fuzzy-number-valued  function $s(x)$ is slowly decreasing
conclusions: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $t_0\geq0$ and  $0<\lambda<1$ such that for every $t>t_0$ $s(t)\succeq s(x)-\overline{\varepsilon} \qquad \textrm{whenever}\qquad  \lambda t< x\leq t.$

nodes.name: Proof of the left-window form of slow decrease
nodes.statement: The proof of the lemma is done by contradiction method. Assume that the fuzzy-number-valued function $s(x)$ is slowly decreasing and there exists $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that for all $0<\lambda<1$ and $t_0\geq0$ there exist real numbers $x$ and $t>t_0$ for which \begin{eqnarray} s(t)\nsucceq s(x)-\overline{\varepsilon}_0\qquad \textrm{whenever}\qquad  \lambda t< x\leq t. \end{eqnarray} Therefore, there exists $\alpha_{\scriptscriptstyle 0}\in [0,1]$ such that \begin{eqnarray} s^-_{\alpha_{ 0}}(t)<s^-_{\alpha_{ 0}}(x)-\varepsilon_0 \quad or\quad s^+_{\alpha_0}(t)<s^+_{\alpha_0}(x)-\varepsilon_0. \end{eqnarray} At this point we recall the reformulated condition of M$\acute{o}$ricz \cite{moric1} for a slowly decreasing real valued function $f$ such that \begin{eqnarray} \lim_{\lambda\rightarrow 1^{-}}\liminf_{t\rightarrow\infty}\min_{\lambda t\leq x\leq t}[f(t)-f(x)]\geq0. \end{eqnarray} No matter which case we choose in (\ref{cases}), one of the real valued functions $s^-_{\alpha_{ 0}}(t)$ and $s^+_{\alpha_0}(t)$ does not satisfy the condition (\ref{soldan}). So at least one of them is not slowly decreasing which contradicts the hypothesis that fuzzy-number-valued function $s(x)$ is slowly decreasing.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: a failure of the left-window inequality produces a level $\alpha_0$ whose endpoint function violates M\'{o}ricz's slow-decrease condition.

nodes.name: Negate the conclusion
nodes.statement: The proof of the lemma is done by contradiction method. Assume that the fuzzy-number-valued function $s(x)$ is slowly decreasing and there exists $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that for all $0<\lambda<1$ and $t_0\geq0$ there exist real numbers $x$ and $t>t_0$ for which \begin{eqnarray} s(t)\nsucceq s(x)-\overline{\varepsilon}_0\qquad \textrm{whenever}\qquad  \lambda t< x\leq t. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Assume slow decrease but suppose the left-window inequality fails for some $\varepsilon_0>0$.

nodes.name: Extract a bad level $\alpha_0$
nodes.statement: Therefore, there exists $\alpha_{\scriptscriptstyle 0}\in [0,1]$ such that \begin{eqnarray} s^-_{\alpha_{ 0}}(t)<s^-_{\alpha_{ 0}}(x)-\varepsilon_0 \quad or\quad s^+_{\alpha_0}(t)<s^+_{\alpha_0}(x)-\varepsilon_0. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Translate the order failure into a strict inequality for one endpoint function at some level $\alpha_0$.

nodes.name: Recall M\'{o}ricz's reformulated condition
nodes.statement: At this point we recall the reformulated condition of M$\acute{o}$ricz \cite{moric1} for a slowly decreasing real valued function $f$ such that \begin{eqnarray} \lim_{\lambda\rightarrow 1^{-}}\liminf_{t\rightarrow\infty}\min_{\lambda t\leq x\leq t}[f(t)-f(x)]\geq0. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Invoke the real-valued reformulation of slow decrease as a $\liminf$ condition on left windows.

nodes.name: Derive the contradiction in either case
nodes.statement: No matter which case we choose in (\ref{cases}), one of the real valued functions $s^-_{\alpha_{ 0}}(t)$ and $s^+_{\alpha_0}(t)$ does not satisfy the condition (\ref{soldan}). So at least one of them is not slowly decreasing which contradicts the hypothesis that fuzzy-number-valued function $s(x)$ is slowly decreasing.
nodes.statement_short: Either case makes an endpoint function fail slow decrease, contradicting the hypothesis.

nodes.name: Slow decrease implies the Tauberian conditions (*) and (**)
nodes.statement: It is clear that if function $s$ is slowly decreasing then conditions (\ref{*}) and (\ref{**}) are satisfied by $(i)$ and $(v)$ of Theorem \ref{bessart}.
nodes.statement_short: Slow decrease of $s$ yields both window-average Tauberian conditions, via linearity and monotonicity of the fuzzy integral.
conclusions: conditions (\ref{*}) and (\ref{**}) are satisfied by $(i)$ and $(v)$ of Theorem \ref{bessart}

nodes.name: Schmidt type slow decrease Tauberian theorem for fuzzy integrals
nodes.statement: If $f$ is a continuous fuzzy-number-valued function such that integral (\ref{integral}) is Ces\`{a}ro summable to a fuzzy number $L$ and its integral function $s(t)$ is slowly decreasing, then the integral (\ref{integral}) converges to $L$.
nodes.statement_short: Slow decrease of $s$ is a Tauberian condition: Ces\`{a}ro summability plus slow decrease gives convergence to $L$.
assumptions: integral (\ref{integral}) is Ces\`{a}ro summable to a fuzzy number $L$
its integral function $s(t)$ is slowly decreasing

nodes.name: Landau type condition implies slow decrease of $s$
nodes.statement: Let $f$ be a continuous fuzzy-number-valued function on $[0,\infty)$. If there exist negative constant fuzzy number $u$ and a real number $x_0\geq 0$ such that \begin{eqnarray} xf(x)\succeq u \quad \textrm{for}\quad x>x_0, \end{eqnarray} then fuzzy-number-valued function $s(t)=\int\limits_{0}^{t}f(x)dx$ is slowly decreasing.
nodes.statement_short: A one-sided Landau bound $xf(x)\succeq u$ for large $x$ forces the integral function $s$ to be slowly decreasing.
assumptions: Let $f$ be a continuous fuzzy-number-valued function on $[0,\infty)$.
there exist negative constant fuzzy number $u$ and a real number $x_0\geq 0$ such that $xf(x)\succeq u \quad \textrm{for}\quad x>x_0$

nodes.name: Proof that the Landau type condition implies slow decrease
nodes.statement: Let $ xf(x)\succeq u$ be satisfied under the given conditions on $u$ and $x_0$ in the theorem. Then for $x>x_0$ we have \begin{eqnarray*} xf_{\alpha}^-(x)\geq u^-_{\alpha}\geq u^-_{0}\qquad ,\qquad xf_{\alpha}^+(x)\geq u^+_{\alpha}\geq u^+_{1}\geq u^-_{0}. \end{eqnarray*} For the sake of simplicity let take $u^-_{0}=-H$ where $H> 0$. Then \begin{eqnarray*} xf_{\alpha}^-(x)\geq -H \Rightarrow f_{\alpha}^-(x)\geq -\frac{H}{x}\quad ,\quad xf_{\alpha}^+(x)\geq -H \Rightarrow f_{\alpha}^+(x)\geq -\frac{H}{x} \end{eqnarray*} are satisfied. Then for $x_0< t<x\leq \lambda t$ when $\lambda>1$, we have \begin{eqnarray*} s_{\alpha}^-(x)-s_{\alpha}^-(t)=\int_t^xf_{\alpha}^-(u)du\geq -H\int_t^x\frac{du}{u}=-H\ln\frac{x}{t}\geq -H\ln \lambda \end{eqnarray*} and \begin{eqnarray*} s_{\alpha}^+(x)-s_{\alpha}^+(t)=\int_t^xf_{\alpha}^+(u)du\geq -H\int_t^x\frac{du}{u}=-H\ln\frac{x}{t}\geq -H\ln \lambda. \end{eqnarray*} Choosing $\lambda =e^{\varepsilon/H}$, we get the inequalities \begin{eqnarray*} s_{\alpha}^-(x)\geq s_{\alpha}^-(t)-\varepsilon\qquad ,\qquad s_{\alpha}^+(x)\geq s_{\alpha}^+(t)-\varepsilon \end{eqnarray*} and then $s(x)\succeq s(t)-\overline{\varepsilon}$ holds whenever $x_0< t<x\leq \lambda t$.
nodes.statement_short: Levelwise: convert $xf(x)\succeq u$ into $f^{\pm}_{\alpha}(x)\geq -H/x$, integrate to get a $-H\ln\lambda$ drop bound, then choose $\lambda=e^{\varepsilon/H}$.

nodes.name: Pass to level endpoint inequalities
nodes.statement: Let $ xf(x)\succeq u$ be satisfied under the given conditions on $u$ and $x_0$ in the theorem. Then for $x>x_0$ we have \begin{eqnarray*} xf_{\alpha}^-(x)\geq u^-_{\alpha}\geq u^-_{0}\qquad ,\qquad xf_{\alpha}^+(x)\geq u^+_{\alpha}\geq u^+_{1}\geq u^-_{0}. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Set up: rewrite the fuzzy order hypothesis as uniform lower bounds on the level endpoint functions.

nodes.name: Introduce $H$ and derive $f^{\pm}_{\alpha}(x)\geq -H/x$
nodes.statement: For the sake of simplicity let take $u^-_{0}=-H$ where $H> 0$. Then \begin{eqnarray*} xf_{\alpha}^-(x)\geq -H \Rightarrow f_{\alpha}^-(x)\geq -\frac{H}{x}\quad ,\quad xf_{\alpha}^+(x)\geq -H \Rightarrow f_{\alpha}^+(x)\geq -\frac{H}{x} \end{eqnarray*} are satisfied.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $H>0$ with $u_0^-=-H$ and divide by $x$ to get the $-H/x$ lower bounds.

nodes.name: Integrate to bound the drop by $-H\ln\lambda$
nodes.statement: Then for $x_0< t<x\leq \lambda t$ when $\lambda>1$, we have \begin{eqnarray*} s_{\alpha}^-(x)-s_{\alpha}^-(t)=\int_t^xf_{\alpha}^-(u)du\geq -H\int_t^x\frac{du}{u}=-H\ln\frac{x}{t}\geq -H\ln \lambda \end{eqnarray*} and \begin{eqnarray*} s_{\alpha}^+(x)-s_{\alpha}^+(t)=\int_t^xf_{\alpha}^+(u)du\geq -H\int_t^x\frac{du}{u}=-H\ln\frac{x}{t}\geq -H\ln \lambda. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the $-H/u$ bound over $[t,x]\subseteq[t,\lambda t]$ to bound the decrease by $-H\ln\lambda$.

nodes.name: Choose $\lambda=e^{\varepsilon/H}$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Choosing $\lambda =e^{\varepsilon/H}$, we get the inequalities \begin{eqnarray*} s_{\alpha}^-(x)\geq s_{\alpha}^-(t)-\varepsilon\qquad ,\qquad s_{\alpha}^+(x)\geq s_{\alpha}^+(t)-\varepsilon \end{eqnarray*} and then $s(x)\succeq s(t)-\overline{\varepsilon}$ holds whenever $x_0< t<x\leq \lambda t$.
nodes.statement_short: Pick $\lambda=e^{\varepsilon/H}$ so the drop is at most $\varepsilon$, giving slow decrease of $s$.

nodes.name: Fuzzy function satisfying the Landau type condition
nodes.statement: Let the fuzzy-number-valued function $f :[0,\infty)\to E^1$ be given as \begin{eqnarray*} (f(x))(t)= \begin{cases} \quad\frac{t}{2-\sin x}\quad, &\quad \textrm{if} \quad   0\leq t\leq 2-\sin x , \\[5pt] 2-\frac{t}{2-\sin x}\ , & \quad  \textrm{if} \quad  2-\sin x\leq t\leq 2(2-\sin x). \end{cases} \end{eqnarray*} Then \begin{eqnarray*} f_{\alpha}^-(x)=(2-\sin x)\alpha \qquad \qquad , \qquad \quad f_{\alpha}^+(x)=(2-\sin x)(2-\alpha). \end{eqnarray*} Since $f_{\alpha}^{\pm}(x)\geq 0$ holds for each $\alpha \in [0,1]$ and $x>0$, we have \begin{eqnarray*} xf_{\alpha}^-(x)\geq 0 \qquad , \qquad xf_{\alpha}^+(x)\geq 0 \quad \end{eqnarray*} which means that $xf(x)\succeq \overline{0}$. So $s(t)$ is slowly decreasing.
nodes.statement_short: A nonnegative triangular fuzzy function based on $2-\sin x$ satisfies $xf(x)\succeq\overline{0}$, so its integral function is slowly decreasing.

nodes.name: Landau type one-sided Tauberian theorem for fuzzy integrals
nodes.statement: If $f$ is a continuous fuzzy-number-valued function  such that integral (\ref{integral}) is Ces\`{a}ro summable to a fuzzy number L and condition (\ref{one}) is satisfied, then the integral (\ref{integral}) converges to $L$.
nodes.statement_short: Ces\`{a}ro summability plus the Landau condition $xf(x)\succeq u$ implies convergence of the improper fuzzy integral to $L$.
assumptions: integral (\ref{integral}) is Ces\`{a}ro summable to a fuzzy number L

nodes.name: Extension to Ces\`{a}ro summability of functions
nodes.statement: We note that one may extend Ces\`{a}ro summability method to continuous fuzzy-number-valued functions and give analogs of Theorem \ref{regular}--\ref{maintheorem}, Corollary \ref{maintheorem2} for Ces\`{a}ro summability of fuzzy-number-valued functions. The proofs are done identically by replacing integral function $s$ with general continuous fuzzy-number-valued function in corresponding proofs and hence omitted.
nodes.statement_short: The whole theory transfers verbatim from integral functions $s$ to arbitrary continuous fuzzy-number-valued functions, with proofs omitted.

nodes.name: Regularity of Ces\`{a}ro summability for fuzzy-number-valued functions
nodes.statement: Let  $f$ be a continuous fuzzy-number-valued function. If \ $\lim_{t\to\infty}f(t)=L$, then $f$ is Ces\`{a}ro summable to fuzzy number $L$.
nodes.statement_short: Convergence of a continuous fuzzy-number-valued function implies its Ces\`{a}ro summability to the same limit.
assumptions: Let  $f$ be a continuous fuzzy-number-valued function.
conclusions: $f$ is Ces\`{a}ro summable to fuzzy number $L$

nodes.name: Necessary and sufficient Tauberian condition for Ces\`{a}ro summable fuzzy functions
nodes.statement: If a continuous fuzzy-number-valued function $f$ is Ces\`{a}ro summable to a fuzzy number $L$, then $\lim_{t\to\infty}f(t)=L$ if and only if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $t_0\geq 0$ and $\lambda>1$ such that for $t> t_0$ \begin{eqnarray*} \frac{1}{\lambda t-t}\int_t^{\lambda t}f(x)dx \succeq f(t)-\overline{\varepsilon} \end{eqnarray*} and another $0<\ell<1$ such that \begin{eqnarray*} \frac{1}{t-\ell t}\int_{\ell t}^{ t}f(x)dx \preceq f(t)+\overline{\varepsilon}. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Function analogue of the main theorem: Ces\`{a}ro summable $f$ converges to $L$ exactly under the two one-sided window-average conditions on $f$.
assumptions: a continuous fuzzy-number-valued function $f$ is Ces\`{a}ro summable to a fuzzy number $L$
conclusions: $\lim_{t\to\infty}f(t)=L$ if and only if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $t_0\geq 0$ and $\lambda>1$ such that for $t> t_0$ $\frac{1}{\lambda t-t}\int_t^{\lambda t}f(x)dx \succeq f(t)-\overline{\varepsilon}$ and another $0<\ell<1$ such that $\frac{1}{t-\ell t}\int_{\ell t}^{ t}f(x)dx \preceq f(t)+\overline{\varepsilon}.$

nodes.name: Slow decrease Tauberian theorem for Ces\`{a}ro summable fuzzy functions
nodes.statement: If a continuous fuzzy-number-valued function $f$ is Ces\`{a}ro summable to a fuzzy number $L$ and $f$ is slowly decreasing, then $\lim_{t\to\infty}f(t)=L$.
nodes.statement_short: Function analogue of the slow-decrease Tauberian theorem: summability plus slow decrease gives $f(t)\to L$.
assumptions: a continuous fuzzy-number-valued function $f$ is Ces\`{a}ro summable to a fuzzy number $L$
